title: 100+ Wedding Captions for Instagram: Sweet, Funny and Short
h1: Wedding Captions for Instagram: 100+ Sweet, Funny and Short Ideas
description: Find the perfect wedding captions for Instagram: 100+ short, romantic, funny and guest-friendly captions for getting ready, the ceremony, reception and more.
excerpt: One hundred wedding captions for Instagram, from short and sweet to funny and heartfelt, for couples, guests, getting ready and the dance floor.
intro:
You've planned the flowers, the seating chart and the first dance. Then the photos start rolling in, and suddenly the hardest decision of the whole wedding is what to write under them. It's a lot of pressure for a little text box.

This list of 100 wedding captions for Instagram is here to help. They're grouped by moment and mood: short and simple, romantic, funny, getting ready, ceremony and "I do," reception and dance floor, newlyweds and honeymoon, and captions for guests and the wedding party. Pick one as is, or tweak it with your names, your date or an inside joke to make it unmistakably yours.
body:

Wedding captions for guests

Attending a wedding? These are perfect for celebrating friends and family.

  1. Celebrating love with the best people.
  2. So happy for these two lovebirds.
  3. Witnessed a fairytale today.
  4. When your best friend marries their best friend.
  5. Here for the love, staying for the cake.

  8. Love is in the air, and so is the confetti.
  9. The cutest couple said "I do" today.
  10. Cried at the vows, crushed it on the dance floor.
  11. Wedding season, but make it fashion.
  12. Honored to celebrate these two.

Tips for writing your own wedding captions

  • Personalize it. Add your names, wedding date, a custom hashtag or a nod to how you met. A caption like "From a coffee shop meet-cute to forever" tells your story in one line.
  • Match the caption to the photo. Save romantic captions for the sunset portrait and funny ones for the candid of your uncle on the dance floor.
  • Keep it short for carousels. If you're posting a gallery, a short caption lets the photos shine. Use the longer, heartfelt ones for a single standout image.
  • Credit your vendors. Tag your photographer, florist and venue. It's a kind gesture and helps small businesses.
  • Respect your guests. Ask before posting close-up photos of guests, especially kids, and follow any unplugged-ceremony wishes.
Tip: Create a simple wedding hashtag using your last name or a playful pun, and share it on your signage or invitations. It makes it easy to find every guest photo afterward.

Want captions for the rest of the year? Our cute couple captions are perfect for date nights and anniversaries, and our anniversary wishes for husband and wife will come in handy a year from now.

Share your love story

The perfect wedding captions for Instagram don't need to be poetic. They just need to capture how the day felt. Pick a few favorites, personalize them, and let your photos do the rest. For more inspiration, browse our full collection of captions and our wedding articles.
takeaways: Short captions let stunning wedding photos speak for themselves.
Match the caption to the moment: romantic for portraits, funny for candids.
Personalize captions with names, dates, how you met or a custom hashtag.
Tag vendors and respect guests' privacy when posting.

faq.q: What is a good caption for a wedding photo?
faq.a: Simple, heartfelt captions usually work best, like "Forever starts today" or "Married to my best friend." For a personal touch, add your wedding date or a nod to your story. If the photo is playful, a funny caption such as "Officially stuck with each other" fits perfectly.

faq.q: What should I caption my wedding post as a guest?
faq.a: Celebrate the couple and the day. Captions like "So happy for these two lovebirds" or "Cried at the vows, crushed it on the dance floor" work well. Tag the couple and use their wedding hashtag if they have one, and check they're happy with you posting photos.

faq.q: How long should a wedding Instagram caption be?
faq.a: Most wedding captions work best short, one line or a few words, especially for photo carousels. If you want to share something more heartfelt, like a note to your new spouse, a longer caption is fine for a single standout image. Keep the first line strong since it shows before the cutoff.

faq.q: Should I use a hashtag for my wedding?
faq.a: A custom hashtag is a great way to gather all your guests' photos in one place. Create something simple using your names or a fun pun, check that it's not already widely used, and share it on signage or invitations so guests remember to use it.
